# M3-CRETE

> Experimental open-source concrete/paste-printing motion-system design for qualified technical users. Cartesian dual-Y belt-pinion architecture with quad-Z self-tramming. Published alongside CEMFORGE materials-evidence and decision-support work; neither system establishes physical suitability without validation. Maintained by Sunnyday Technologies LLC, Appleton WI.

This file is a high-density, plain-text summary intended for LLM retrieval and RAG indexing. Authoritative source is the GitHub repository and the JSON BOM linked below.

Important safety and product-boundary note: M3-CRETE is intended for qualified technical users, R&D labs, supervised institutional programs, and experienced builders. It is not a casual hobby kit, toy, finished certified printer, certified construction machine, turnkey jobsite system, or structural concrete production system. Public project files may identify electrical interfaces, low-voltage controls, and component references, but they are not AC mains wiring instructions.

## Identity

- Project name: M3-CRETE (Mobile, Modular, Meter³)
- Live site: https://m3-crete.com
- Repository: https://github.com/sunnyday-technologies/M3-CRETE
- License: CERN-OHL-W-2.0 (CAD/Components/ subdirectory: CC BY-SA 4.0)
- Maintainer: Sunnyday Technologies LLC (https://sunn3d.com)
- Contact: m3@sunn3d.com

## Models

- M3-1 — 1000 × 1000 × 1000 mm build volume; no axis splice; all single-piece extrusions.
- M3-2 — 2000 × 1000 × 1000 mm build volume; X-axis spliced. Default build target.
- M3-4 — 2000 × 2000 × 1000 mm build volume; both X and Y spliced.

Variant parameters (quantity overrides) are defined in https://bom.m3-crete.com/config.js under MODEL_VARIANTS.

## Architecture (M3-2 default)

- Frame: 4080 C-Beam primary structure (Z-posts, Y-gantry rails) plus 2040 bracing. All 1000 mm standard lengths. C opening points inward toward the cube.
- X-axis: 2× 1000 mm 4080 spliced = 2000 mm envelope. Splice uses straight-line slot-linking kit with internal 2040 reinforcement bonded inside the C-channel.
- Y-axis: 2× parallel 2080 rails, 1000 mm span, dual motors (anti-racking).
- Z-axis: 4× independent belt-driven 2040 vertical posts (quad self-tramming via Klipper Z_TILT_ADJUST).
- Motion: GT2 10 mm belt + polycarbonate V-wheels on all axes.
- Motors: 7× NEMA23 8 mm shaft (1× X + 2× Y + 4× Z) + 1× extruder (NEMA34, owner-supplied).
- Controller: BTT Kraken (8× TMC5160 onboard) + Raspberry Pi 5 + Klipper.
- Homing: StallGuard4 sensorless via TMC5160 (no mechanical limit switches).
- Printhead target: 1.5 kg, 1″ Male NPT pipe connection, counter-weighted hose.
- Open BOM component target: under USD 5,000 when self-sourced and self-assembled, where current commodity pricing and substitutions allow. This is a self-sourced component target, not a Sunnyday sale price.

## Safety and electrical boundary

- Any AC mains wiring, control-box integration, grounding, bonding, overcurrent protection, disconnects, emergency-stop power circuits, facility connection, inspection, or code compliance work must be performed by qualified personnel, a licensed electrician where required, or a qualified control-panel shop.
- Public BOM data, build documentation, and component references are not AC mains wiring instructions.

## Out of scope (do not add)

- Mechanical limit switches / endstops — replaced by StallGuard4.
- Mechanical leveling feet — handled by build-plate probing instead.
- External reinforcement on X-gantry beam — would interfere with the 2-sided X-carriage wheel path.
- HEPA filter, carbon-fiber bars, LED lights.
- Pump system — separate proprietary product (NemoCrete), not part of M3-CRETE.

## Bill of Materials

- Source of truth: https://bom.m3-crete.com/bom/data.json (JSON; current snapshot 65 parts, 189 options, 35 named suppliers; verify the live JSON because counts can change).
- Interactive viewer: https://bom.m3-crete.com/bom/
- Viewer features: multi-supplier selection, coverage tracking, per-part quantity adjusters, "I have this" exclusion, Buy/Print/CNC toggle on fabricated parts, CSV/JSON export, model-variant selector (M3-1 / M3-2 / M3-4).

## Companion projects

- CEMFORGE — early-stage materials evidence and decision support; modeled outputs require physical validation and qualified review: https://cemforge.ai
- Open3DCP — public draft schema for recording 3D concrete printing material, process, test, and provenance data; it is not itself a supplied dataset or ratified standard: https://open3dcp.org

## Machine-readable surface

- Sitemap: https://bom.m3-crete.com/sitemap.xml
- robots.txt: https://bom.m3-crete.com/robots.txt (explicitly allows ClaudeBot, GPTBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot)
- Experimental site manifest for this BOM/documentation host: https://bom.m3-crete.com/.well-known/mcp-manifest.json
- CreativeWork JSON-LD: embedded in https://bom.m3-crete.com/ inside a `<script type="application/ld+json">` tag.

## Status

Active development. Development CAD and the reference BOM are published; build guides and assembly documentation are added as they are reviewed. Publication or review does not mean the machine, assembly, electrical system, safety function, or material process has been physically validated, certified, or approved for a project.
